title: Your Window Spider Has 8 Eyes 👀 (Things Living In Your House #48)
pinned_comment: Be honest: do you let the jumping spider on your window stay, or jar it outside? 🕷️ stay / 🫙 jar

source_quotes.ucipm: UC IPM Pest Notes: Spiders. Salticidae, jumping spiders: Day-active hunters in plants or on the ground. They make no web; instead they stalk and pounce on prey by jumping distances many times their body length. Jumping spiders have a distinctive pattern of eyes in three rows: the first row of four eyes, with large and distinctive middle eyes; a second row of two very small to minute eyes; and a third row of two medium sized pairs of eyes. (4 + 2 + 2 = 8 eyes)
source_quotes.mdc: Missouri Conservationist (Oct 2024), Life on a Thread: The large eyes empower jumpers with the highest visual resolution of any animal less than 20 millimeters long. In fact, a jumping spider's vision is comparable to much larger animals like pigeons or dogs. / Some species ... can leap horizontally up to 40 body lengths.
source_quotes.usu: Utah State University Extension, Jumping Spiders (Salticidae): often found on walls (indoors and outdoors) ... Diet: insects and spiders. Significance: could be a nuisance pest indoors; not known to be a health hazard; beneficial.
